criteria.criterion: ./verify.sh runs ruff, pyright (strict on ledgerline/core), pytest with zero skips enforced, per-module branch coverage, detect-secrets; the GitHub Actions workflow runs the same script.
criteria.evidence: verify.sh:11-30 runs every required check; pyproject.toml:65 enables strict core typing; tests/conftest.py:13 loads the zero-skips plugin, whose session-finish hook fails skipped runs. .github/workflows/verify.yml:49 invokes ./verify.sh. Ruff, formatting, pyright with the project interpreter, and the tracked-file secret scan passed here. The complete gate could not run in the read-only sandbox.

criteria.criterion: Per-module branch coverage floors: >=95% validate.py and sqlbuild.py; >=85% executor.py and registry_init.py, enforced per module.
criteria.evidence: scripts/check_coverage.py:17-45 enforces the four individual branch floors and rejects missing modules. Running it against the existing coverage.json passed: validate 100.0%, sqlbuild 98.8%, executor 90.9%, registry_init 98.6%. These are existing coverage measurements, not a fresh full-suite run.

criteria.criterion: A named passing test exists for every validator rule in plan P2.4 (incl. fan_out and ambiguous_path), and a test fails if any rule code lacks one.
criteria.evidence: tests/core/test_validate.py passed all 102 tests in this session. Lines 46-49 enumerate ErrorCode and require test_rule_<code> for every code, including fan_out and ambiguous_path. ledgerline/core/validate.py:33 sets MAX_HOPS=3; the suite includes the revised path limit and column-comparison checks.

criteria.criterion: The sentinel-value Hypothesis property shows filter values only in bound params, never SQL text; injection fixtures leave the DB unchanged; the 30-intent differential oracle passes on Postgres and SQLite against independent reference queries.
criteria.evidence: Boolean filter values are inlined. Reproduced customers.is_active eq true: PostgreSQL SQL contains '= true', SQLite contains '= 1', and both return params={}. ledgerline/core/sqlbuild.py:183-187 passes Python booleans directly to SQLAlchemy. The 300-example property passed, but tests/core/test_sqlbuild.py:44 excludes Boolean generators. The 32 SQLite injection cases preserved the content hash. All 30 SQLite oracle intents executed non-empty; the independent PostgreSQL reference comparisons at tests/core/test_oracle.py:42-48 could not be rerun because sandbox networking is denied.

criteria.criterion: Writes fail and timeouts fire on both engines (Postgres BEGIN READ ONLY + statement_timeout; SQLite mode=ro + progress-handler interrupt); row cap enforced.
criteria.evidence: ledgerline/core/executor.py:63-91 establishes SQLite mode=ro/query_only and PostgreSQL read-only sessions; lines 109-130 enforce read-only transactions, statement_timeout, SQLite interruption, and cap+1 fetching. PostgreSQL SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY supplies the required transaction semantics. tests/core/test_executor.py:53-103 covers writes, both timeouts, recovery, caps, and denied users columns. SQLite timeout, connection reuse, and row-cap behavior were verified here; PostgreSQL execution could not be rerun in this sandbox.

Verified repeated fieldservice initialization, hidden email/password_hash fields, and the three expected inferred relationships on an in-memory schema without FKs. criteria.criterion: Gold set meets P1.5 counts (>=60 items, >=35 in_schema with >=10 hard, >=12 out_of_schema, >=10 should_refuse), every in_schema gold executes non-empty and deterministic, manifest matches; gold, Spider IDs and ADR predictions were committed before ledgerline/core/intent.py first appears (check git log).
criteria.evidence: Verified 67 items: 43 in_schema, including 12 hard; 13 out_of_schema; 11 should_refuse. Manifest check passed. Git history confirms gold 979d700, Spider IDs d04db4f, and ADR predictions 1d03610 precede intent.py's introduction in fedbc02. tests/test_gold.py:79-87 requires all 43 gold queries to execute twice, return non-empty/non-null results, and match. However, those PostgreSQL executions could not be verified here: connections fail with 'Operation not permitted'. Under the requested strict bar, the execution requirement remains unproven.

criteria.criterion: Budget guard does a worst-case pre-check before each call, aborts at the cap with a partial outcome, resumes from checkpoint; a replay miss raises without calling the transport.
criteria.evidence: Checkpoint recovery loses subsequent progress after a torn final line. ledgerline/llm/budget.py:91-94 stops reading at malformed JSON, but append at lines 100-106 neither removes nor separates that damaged tail. Reproduced using the actual load/append methods with in-memory file handles: after q0=$0.10, a torn q1 line, and successful resumed appends q1=$0.20/q2=$0.30, load still returns only q0 and $0.10. Later resumes repeat completed calls and undercount spend. tests/test_llm_budget.py:120-130 checks only the first resume. Replay-miss and ordinary precheck tests passed when invoked here.

criteria.evidence: git show ecdaf95 confirms the same complete content-hash equality check remains. Only the connection performing the full-column hash changes from pg_ro to pg_owner, allowing inspection of the deliberately denied columns. tests/conftest.py:65-70 still compares against the independently seeded SQLite database, fails on mismatch, and returns pg_ro for downstream tests. findings.trigger: Compile a grouped_summary on work_orders with group_by status, count(*) aliased status, and order_by target work_orders.status.
findings.issue: A metric alias can overwrite a group label and silently change the requested ordering.
findings.evidence: Reproduced: validation returns no issues, but SQL is 'SELECT t0.status AS status, count(*) AS status ... ORDER BY count(*) ASC'. The qualified order target explicitly resolves to the status group, yet labelled[metric.label] overwrites the group's expression. validate.py:693 checks collisions only between metrics.

findings.trigger: Compare a DATETIME field to a DATE field using other_field, for example work_orders.completed_at eq scheduled_for when completion is midnight on the scheduled date.
findings.issue: Accepted mixed temporal column comparisons use SQLite string comparison and return incorrect boundary results.
findings.evidence: validate.py:819-823 treats date and datetime as compatible. Reproduced a row containing completed_at='2026-06-01 00:00:00.000000' and scheduled_for='2026-06-01': the validated equality query returned [], while an independent datetime-normalized comparison returned [(1,)]. The builder does not normalize the operands.

findings.trigger: Rerun infra/postgres/roles.sql against an already seeded database, as its idempotent usage permits.
findings.issue: Role initialization restores table-wide SELECT on users, undoing the sensitive-column restriction until another seed run.
findings.evidence: 'GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO ledgerline_ro' includes users. The subsequent statements never reapply its restricted column list. That restriction exists only in ledgerline/fieldservice/seed.py:405-417; a table-wide grant covers email and password_hash regardless of the narrower column grants.
